title: Percentile
summary: The value at a chosen percentile of the source over a rolling window, drawn on the price chart, interpolated between the two nearest ranks.
descriptionHtml:
The Percentile study sorts the last Period values of the source and plots the value at the chosen percentile. The rank is the percentile as a fraction times one less than the number of values, and when that rank falls between two positions the study interpolates linearly between the two neighbouring values.

A percentile of 50 gives the median, 0 gives the lowest value in the window and 100 the highest. The default of 25 traces the lower quartile, a level that about a quarter of the recent source values sit below.

The study answers from the first bar, ranking however many bars exist until the window fills, and it skips absent values.
howToReadHtml:
Read the line as a floor or ceiling drawn from the distribution of recent prices rather than from a single extreme. A low percentile marks where price has rarely traded in the window, and a close below it is unusual for the period. A high percentile does the same for the top.

Two copies of the study, one at a low and one at a high percentile, make a band that ignores single outlier bars, unlike a channel built from the window's highest and lowest values. Like any rolling statistic it trails a fast move.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series whose values are ranked.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: How many recent bars are ranked. A longer period gives a steadier level.

settings.label: percentile
settings.html: Which percentile to draw, from 0 for the window low to 100 for the window high; 50 is the median.

faq.q: How is it different from the window's lowest value?
faq.html: The lowest value is set by a single bar. A low percentile such as 10 or 25 ignores the few most extreme bars, so one spike does not move it.

faq.q: Why is the setting labelled in lower case?
faq.html: The setting is stored under the name percentile, which is also the name of a built-in function, so its label carries that name directly. It still accepts any value from 0 to 100.
When the chosen percentile falls between two ranked values, the line sits proportionally between them instead of jumping from one to the other, so it moves more smoothly.

related.title: Polynomial Fitting (POLYFIT)
related.summary: Fits a least-squares polynomial of the chosen degree to the recent window and plots the fitted curve's value at the current bar.

related.title: Mode
related.summary: The value that repeats most often in the recent window, drawn only when some value actually repeats, marking prices the market keeps returning to.

related.title: Quantile (QUANTILE)
related.summary: The requested quantile of the source over a rolling window, drawn on the price chart: 0.5 is the rolling median, 0 the low, 1 the high.
